page.h1: Best power bank for your phone
page.desc: A 10,000 mAh USB-C bank fits a phone, but iPhone 17 needs 40 W and 45 W Galaxy models need PPS. Which 10K banks from Anker, INIU, Baseus and Belkin hit each phone's tier.
page.answer: Short answer. A 10000mAh USB-C phone power bank is the right size, but 20 W is not: iPhone 17 needs a 40 W source and Galaxy Plus/Ultra 45 W with PPS. The Anker Nano Power Bank 10K 45W states 40 W for iPhone 17 and 45 W for Samsung; Baseus PicoGo AM52 adds Qi2.2 25 W wireless.

page.after:
What the differences mean

The common advice to buy any USB-C PD bank of 20 W or more is right for some phones and wrong for the newest ones. Apple's fast-charge support page (updated 22 Oct 2026) says the iPhone 17, 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max reach 50% in about 20 minutes only with a 40 W or higher adapter; the iPhone Air and 17e need 20 W or higher; the iPhone 15 and 16 need an 18 W or greater USB-PD source. A 20 W bank therefore meets the Air, 17e, 15 and 16 tier and misses the 17 and 17 Pro tier. Samsung's support page adds a second rule: Super Fast Charging switches on only when the source supports USB PD PPS, however high its wattage label, and Samsung's compatibility chart gives 45 W Super Fast Charging 2.0 only to the S24+, S24 Ultra, S25+, S25 Ultra, S26+ and S26 Ultra, with the base S24, S25, S26, FE and Edge models capped at 25 W.

Delivered capacity is the same story for every 10,000 mAh bank here. Engadget's tests put about 5,800 mAh into the phone from a 10,000 mAh pack. Against Apple's EU-label capacities that is 5,800 ÷ 3,692 = 1.6 charges of an iPhone 17, 5,800 ÷ 4,252 = 1.4 of a 17 Pro and 5,800 ÷ 5,088 = 1.1 of a 17 Pro Max, so a 5,000 mAh bank would not fill a Pro Max once.

Charging two things at once also changes the answer. Anker's spec for the Nano 10K 45W is 15 W on the cable plus 7.5 W on the port when both are in use, 15 + 7.5 = 22.5 W total, so with earbuds on the port the phone sits below Apple's 18 W threshold. The 45 W and 40 W figures hold only with the phone alone.

Which bank fast-charges which phone

Anker Nano Power Bank 10K 45W. Anker's product page is the only one in this group that states a per-phone figure: 'Only the USB-C port / cable supports 45W max output for Samsung and 40W max output for iPhone 17 series', and only the USB-C cable and port support Samsung Fast Charging 2.0. The output table runs 5V⎓3A through 20V⎓2.25A, input is 30 W max, weight is 0.51 lb. Gigazine measured 34 to 36 W into a Pixel 10 Pro XL and a 160-minute recharge at 29 W, so the 45 W label is a ceiling rather than a typical phone number. Anker also notes that iPhone 14 and earlier need a USB-C to Lightning adapter that is not in the box. {buy:anker-nano-power-bank-10k-45w-a1638}

Baseus PicoGo AM52 Qi2.2. Baseus lists 45 W through the built-in cable, Qi2.2-certified 25 W magnetic wireless, 30 W self-recharge and about 202 g. Apple's iPhone 17 specification lists Qi2 wireless charging up to 25 W, and Apple's support page caps the iPhone 15 and earlier at 15 W wireless, so the Qi2.2 tier pays off on the iPhone 16 and 17 and not on older models. Baseus's own FAQ puts usable capacity at about 5,500 to 6,500 mAh, in line with Engadget's measured 5,800. It is the pick for an iPhone 16 or 17 owner who wants to drop the phone on the bank without a cable, and it costs $55.99 today against $89.99 list. {buy:baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w}

INIU Pocket Rocket Mini P50-E1. INIU's page names 'Samsung Super Fast Charging 2.0 (PPS)' and 45 W, which is the exact requirement Samsung sets for its Plus and Ultra phones, at 160 g and $32.99. The lanyard USB-C cable detaches, so it also works with a Lightning cable for older iPhones.

INIU Carry P55L-E2. Same 45 W PD headline for $26.99 with a built-in lanyard cable, but INIU lists only PD and QC for this model, so count on it for the 20 W-tier iPhones and the 25 W Galaxy tier rather than 45 W Super Fast Charging 2.0.

INIU SnapGo P73-E1. Qi2 15 W magnetic plus 45 W wired from two USB-C ports at $39.99. Its 15 W wireless is the tier Apple assigns to the iPhone 15 and earlier, so it suits those phones; an iPhone 16 or 17 leaves 10 W of wireless speed on the table compared with the Baseus.

Not recommended

Belkin BoostCharge 10K with integrated cable is well built but tops out at 20 W for $24.99, while the INIU Carry P55L-E2 gives 45 W for $26.99. Its 2.2 in cable also means the phone has to sit on the bank.

Any Anker 10,000 mAh 22.5 W bank with a built-in cable sold without a model number. Notebookcheck reported Anker's 2025 recall of about 481,000 power banks after 33 fire or explosion reports, and the A1257 10,000 mAh model is on that list. Check the model number printed on the back before buying a 22.5 W Anker 10K, and register any A1257 with Anker's recall programme.
